# Shared brief: michi hardening trails (read fully)

Repo /Users/gabe/Projects/michi (Rust workspace; `michi-core` FSL, `michi-graph` MIT no_std, `michi-pipeline` async, NAPI shim in `packages/michi-node`, its exports in `crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs`). 0.10.0 is released; we are pre-1.0 and every consumer is our own repo, so **breaking changes are fine and legacy surface is removed, never shimmed**. Follow `AGENTS.md` and `PRINCIPLES.md`; ADRs and `docs/spec/06-decisions.md` record decisions you must not re-litigate (read headings first).
Four read-only audits produced the findings you act on: `/tmp/claude-501/audit-{architecture,security,rust-perf,duplication}.md`. Your trail names the finding numbers; read those entries (evidence, proposed change, "Not examined") and verify each is still true on current main before changing code. If a finding is wrong or already fixed, say so and skip it.

## Parallel trails, strict ownership (this is how we avoid conflicts)
Other trails run at the same time in other worktrees. Edit only files your trail owns. If your change forces a one-line call-site fix in a file another trail owns (for example `napi.rs`), make the minimal fix and say so in your report. Never reformat or reorganize files you do not own. If `git merge origin/main` brings conflicts in your files, resolve them keeping both sides' intent.
Trails: T1 envelope integrity (core model files, toon/ writers); T2 NAPI structure (`napi.rs` and `packages/michi-node`); T3 release-signing CI (`.github/workflows/callisto-release.yml`, `.prototools`); T4 pipeline error redaction (`crates/michi-pipeline/src/error.rs`, `redact.rs`, `fuzz/`, trust-model docs); T5 docs/tests/CI hygiene (docs drift, new tests, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`); T6 pipeline observers.

## Flow (autonomous; never ask questions; decide and report the decision)
1. `git fetch origin && git checkout -B <your-branch> origin/main` (git network and cargo need `dangerouslyDisableSandbox: true` on that one command; use `$TMPDIR` for temp files; keep commands simple, no computed git arguments).
2. TDD: a failing test first, confirm it fails for the right reason, then fix. For every behavioral claim, break the code on purpose (mutant), watch the test fail, revert. Report the mutants.
3. Update docs/spec for anything you change (CI's "Spec first" job) and rustdoc for every pub item. Add one `.changeset/<slug>.md` for code changes (look at existing ones and `CONTRIBUTING.md`; package `michi-core` unless your change is elsewhere; start a paragraph with `Breaking:` when behavior or API breaks). No changeset for CI-only or docs-only changes.
4. Checks, judged by exit code only: `just fmt-check`, `just clippy`, `just test-rust`, `just typos`, plus `just check` once at the end, plus anything specific to your trail (Node: `pnpm build && pnpm test` in `packages/michi-node`; workflows: `actionlint` and `just zizmor`).
5. Commit (conventional, why-not-what; **no claude.ai session links, no Claude-Session trailer**), push, open a **draft** PR against main with a short plain body (what, why, how checked, what was not run, any decision you made). Never merge, never force-push, never push to main.

## Final message (<= 200 words)
PR URL; per-finding outcome (fixed / skipped with reason); decisions you made; checks with exit codes; mutants run; anything left or surprising.

257:## #9 [M] Module names do not match their contents
280:## #10 [L] Builder and argument conventions are inconsistent, and 1.0 would lock them in
302:## #11 [L] Small model gaps: a dead field, and states the domain forbids

335:## Examined, no finding

64:## #3 [L] No compile-time `Send + Sync` assertions in `michi-pipeline` and `michi-graph`
70:## #4 [L] Source-text scanning tests stand in for compile-time guarantees
78:## #5 [L] `michi-graph` claims `no_std` but is only built for the host

106:## #9 [L] `pub` napi-core functions take owned arguments they do not consume
112:## #10 [L] Benchmark and scaling coverage gaps

### #4 [M] Known leftover `ToonOptions.hints` and `render_parts(inline: bool)`: confirmed, and `hints` is coupled to `truncation_hint`
- Evidence: `ToonOptions.hints` (`toon/mod.rs:145`) is read only by `ToonDocument::render` (`render.rs:415-419`). `AgentResponse` never sets it (`response.rs:240-244` leaves it empty and merges hints itself through `render_parts(false)`'s `extra`). It has 40+ callers: tests (`toon_spec.rs`, `snapshot_tests.rs`, `line_injection.rs`, `proptest_toon.rs`, `toon_integration.rs`, `toon_spec_fixtures.rs`), `examples/basic_toon.rs`, `examples/readme_quickstart.rs`, `benches/toon_render.rs`, `fuzz/fuzz_targets/toon_render.rs`, and the NAPI `renderToon` (`JsToonOptions.hints`, `napi.rs:112`; `renderToon` appears in `index.test.mjs`, `interop.test.mjs`, `scripts/smoke/npm/smoke.cjs`, `packages/michi-node/README.md`, root `README.md`, `docs/spec/04`). `render_parts(inline: bool)` (`render.rs:429`) has two callers: `render()` with `true` and `response.rs:263` with `false`. The flag changes two behaviours at once (whether `truncated` and `totalCount` are inlined, and whether the returned cut list is empty), and the return type is an unnamed 3-tuple `(String, Vec<(usize,String,usize)>, Option<String>)`.
- The coupling: if `hints` is removed, `truncation_hint` still has to put its "Cut cells are listed in the truncated block..." line inside the same `help[]` block as the caller's hints, because a document may hold only one `help` key. That is why `hints` lives on the options today. Removal therefore means either (a) dropping `truncation_hint` from `ToonOptions` too and leaving it to `AgentResponse`, or (b) having the standalone renderer return the extra hint for the caller to append. Option (a) also removes the standalone NAPI `truncationHint`.
- Change (cheapest first): replace `render_parts(bool)` with `fn render_list(&self) -> RenderedList { text, cuts, extra_hint }` (a named `pub(crate)` struct, cuts always returned). `render()` becomes a short composition: truncated block from `cuts`, `totalCount`, then `append_help_block(caller hints + extra)`. That removes the boolean and the "empty vec when inline" case with no API change. Do the `hints` removal only after deciding `truncation_hint` (ADR-worthy, pre-1.0 so cheap).
- Proof: `toon_spec.rs`, `toon_truncation_signal.rs`, `proptest_toon.rs`, `snapshot_toon_basic_list`, `envelope.rs`. The source-grep guard at `render.rs:1100-1109` asserts `proof` holds exactly `["validate","render","render_parts"]`, so it must be updated in the same commit.
- Effort: S for the struct, M for dropping hints. Breaking: struct is `pub(crate)`, so no; dropping `hints` is breaking for Rust and JS. Confidence: high.

### #5 [M] Known leftover public `Section.returned_count` / `Section.truncated`: confirmed vestigial; `BudgetSummary.sections` duplicates the same data by hand
- Evidence: `Section.returned_count` (`section.rs:29`) is ignored for `Toon` and `Kv` bodies (`count()` at `:107` derives it) and consulted only for `Text`. Direct readers of the field: `tests/sections.rs:75,84` only. The setter `.returned_count(n)` is used for `Text` in `tests/envelope.rs:147` and `sections.rs:80`. `Section.truncated` (`:34`) is read by `response.rs:691` (JSON only) and its doc says it "does not change the text render". Nothing outside tests reads either field directly. `docs/spec/03-rust-api.md`, `06-decisions.md` and `07-...envelope.md` mention `returnedCount`.
- The same facts are also modelled as `SectionCost { name, returned, total, truncated }` (`budget.rs:112-122`), which the caller builds by hand and which can disagree with the real `Section`s in the same response (`envelope.rs:253` builds sections and budget independently). Three different things are called "truncated": a cut cell (the `truncated` block), `Section.truncated`, and `BudgetSummary.truncated`.
- Change: make `returned_count` and `truncated` private (or fold `Text`'s count into `SectionBody::Text { text, count }`), keep the builders, read via accessors. Consider deriving the budget `sections` roll-up from the real sections at render time, with the caller supplying only totals michi cannot know. Check wisp/monokl usage first (ADR 10: the envelope is unstable until a second consumer adopts it).
- Steps: a) change the two fields to private plus getters; b) update `sections.rs:75,84` (the `bad in [0, 99]` test becomes unnecessary because the field cannot be hand-edited); c) separately, the roll-up derivation. Proof: `sections.rs`, `envelope.rs`, the `.snap` files, `docs/spec/07`.
- Effort: S for a), M for c). Breaking: removes public fields (`Section` is `#[non_exhaustive]`). Confidence: high on the fields, medium on the roll-up change.

### #6 [L-M] Known leftover `empty_state*` versus an empty `Section`: NOT equivalent today; the surface is 4 Rust fns + 2 NAPI exports
- Evidence: `AgentResponse::new("t").render(Text)` is `t: []` (`tests/envelope.rs:89`); `empty_state("issue")` is `issue: []\ntotalCount: 0` (`tests/toon_blocks.rs:158`, `toon_integration.rs:29`). Dependents: `toon_spec.rs`, `toon_integration.rs`, `toon_blocks.rs`, `snapshot_tests.rs`, `line_injection.rs`, the napi tests (19 `emptyState` refs in `__test__`), README tables.

### #11 [L] Standalone renderers all take `hints` (and `totalCount`) positionally; the composer already owns both
- `render_kv(items, total_count, hints)`, `render_already_done(op, summary, hints)`, `empty_state_with_hints`, `StatusResponse::with_hints`, `ToonOptions.hints`, NAPI `renderKv(items, totalCount, hints)` and `renderToon`. Dependents of `renderKv`: `napi.rs`, `index.test.mjs`, `packages/michi-node/README.md`, `06-decisions.md`, `04-mcp-and-napi.md`. Dependents of `renderToon`: also `interop.test.mjs`, `scripts/smoke/npm/smoke.cjs`, root `README.md`.
- Order: do #4 first, then this. Effort: M. Breaking: Rust and JS. Confidence: medium (design call; check monokl, wisp and caliper callers first).

## #9 [M] Module names do not match their contents

**Evidence**

- `idempotency` holds `PartialSuccess`, `OpRef` and `FailedOp`, and nothing about idempotency. `IdempotencyKey`,
  `AlreadyDone`, `already_done` and `render_already_done` live in `resilience` (`resilience.rs:364-430`). AGENTS.md has
  to carry the line "despite the name, idempotency keys … live in `resilience`".
- `truncate` (`Truncated`, string-level) and `truncation` (`TruncationOutcome`, list-level) are sibling modules whose
  names differ by a suffix.
- Core's `pipeline` module is data and render only. The executor is the `michi-pipeline` crate. It is the same word at
  two layers. This is defensible, since NAPI's `renderPipeline` needs the status vocabulary in core.

**Why it matters.** Module paths are public API. Renaming is a search-and-replace now and a major bump after 1.0. Root
re-exports (`lib.rs`) mean most callers do not notice.

`idempotency` module. Merge `truncate` and `truncation` into one `truncation` module, keeping `Truncated` and
`TruncationOutcome`. Keep root re-exports unchanged.

**Effort** S. **Breaking?** Module paths only; root paths are unchanged. **Confidence** high.

## #10 [L] Builder and argument conventions are inconsistent, and 1.0 would lock them in
## #1 [M] `AgentResponse` deep-clones every row on each validate and each render

Evidence:
- `crates/michi-core/src/response.rs:240`: `section_options` does `ToonOptions::new(name, fields.to_vec(), rows.to_vec())` ("Copies the rows: `ToonOptions` owns them", doc comment above it).
- It is called from `section_part` (:258, once per render), `failed_flags` (:279, called by `is_error()`), and `root_collision` paths, so one `is_error()` plus one `to_call_tool_result()` clones the whole body twice.
- Measured with a counting allocator (scratch crate `ap`; 3 fields, 90-char title cells), release build:

| 1000 rows | time/iter | allocs/iter | bytes/iter |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `render_toon(&opts)` | 70 us | 3 | 138 KB |
| `AgentResponse::render(Text)` | 95 us | 2015 | 393 KB |
| `AgentResponse::is_error()` (documented "validates without rendering") | 27 us | 2011 | 170 KB |
| `AgentResponse::to_call_tool_result()` | 262 us | 2019 | 902 KB |
| `is_error()` + `to_call_tool_result()` | 294 us | 4030 | 1.07 MB |

  At 100 rows: 215 allocs for `render` vs 3 for `render_toon`. About 2 allocations per row come only from the clone (the per-row `Vec` plus the heap `CompactString`s over 24 bytes).

Why it matters: this is the path every MCP tool response takes, and `is_error()` is a validation that allocates a full copy of the data. The time cost is about 35% on `render` and `is_error()` is dominated by it. It also makes peak memory 2-3x the response size.

Change: let `ToonDocument::validate`/`render_parts` work on a borrowed view (`&str` type name, `&[String]` fields, `&[Vec<Value>]` rows, plus the scalar options). `ToonOptions` can build that view from `&self`, and `section_options` becomes a struct of references. Internal change only.

Effort: M. Breaking: no (`ToonDocument` stays opaque; `validate(&ToonOptions)` keeps its signature). Confidence: high (measured).

Related, smaller: `render_parts` capacity guess (`60 + rows * (fields * 12 + 10)`, render.rs ~line 405) was too small for the bench data above (138 KB allocated for a 100 KB result, so it grew). Cheap to improve by summing string lengths, but not worth a finding on its own.

## #7 [L] `toon::list` holds three copies of the data at once

Evidence: `crates/michi-core/src/toon/mod.rs:297-340`. Each item goes `serde_json::to_vec` -> `from_slice` into an `serde_json::Map` (kept in `objects`, with `preserve_order`), and then a second pass builds `Vec<Vec<Value>>` rows, and only then renders. Peak memory is roughly JSON tree + `Value` rows + output. The round trip through text is deliberate (comment about `f32`), so the intent is fine; the retention of `objects` until all rows are built is what can be avoided. Not measured (memory), so **unverified**.

Change: only the field-union needs a first pass; either keep the serialized `Vec<u8>` per item (cheaper than a `Map`) and parse twice, or convert to `Vec<Value>` per item immediately with a growing field map and pad rows at the end. Effort: M. Breaking: no. Confidence: medium.

## #10 [L] Benchmark and scaling coverage gaps

- Benches: only `toon::render_toon`, `kv`, graph and the scheduler. Nothing covers `AgentResponse` (multi-section envelope, `to_call_tool_result`, JSON render), `toon::list` (serde), `DomainError` rendering/redaction, or `truncate*`. #1 above went unnoticed for that reason.
- Scaling tests (`michi-core/tests/scaling.rs`): `render_toon` rows and cell length, kv items, `truncate`, `truncate_by_size`, envelope section count. Missing: `AgentResponse` rows per section, `toon::list` item count, many cut cells (the `cut` vector and `truncated` block), `render_hints` with many hints, redaction on long strings. I did not find a quadratic path in these by reading `push_list`/`push_truncated`/`truncated_table`; this is coverage, not a bug.

Change: add an `AgentResponse::render` + `to_call_tool_result` divan bench with an allocation-count assertion (a counted-allocs test is deterministic, unlike wall time) and the missing scaling cases. Effort: S. Breaking: no. Confidence: high.

[package]
name        = "michi-core"
description = "AXI response primitives for agent-ergonomic tools: TOON lists, key-value blocks, hints, errors, truncation and retry policy"
readme      = "../../README.md"
keywords    = ["axi", "agent", "mcp", "cli", "llm"]
categories  = ["text-processing", "encoding", "development-tools"]
version = "0.10.0"
edition.workspace      = true
rust-version.workspace = true
license.workspace      = true
repository.workspace   = true
homepage.workspace     = true
authors.workspace      = true
documentation          = "https://docs.rs/michi-core"

exclude = ["moon.yml", "tests/"]

[package.metadata.docs.rs]

features     = ["serde", "schemars", "miette"]
rustdoc-args = ["--cfg", "docsrs"]

[lints]
workspace = true

[dependencies]
compact_str = { workspace = true }
thiserror.workspace = true

serde      = { workspace = true, optional = true }
serde_json = { workspace = true, optional = true }
schemars   = { workspace = true, optional = true }
miette     = { workspace = true, optional = true }

napi-derive = { version = "3", optional = true }

[features]
default  = []

napi     = ["dep:napi", "dep:napi-derive", "serde"]

[dev-dependencies]

```text
issues[2]{number,title,state}:
  51815,"[Bug]: Telegram plugin",open
  51812,dark mode request,open
```

On a 100-row uniform list, TOON used a median 47% fewer tokens than pretty-printed JSON (range 20.9 to 50.4% across nine datasets), 23% fewer than minified JSON (-4.3 to 26.8%) and 8% fewer than a Markdown table (0.1 to 20.2%). Counts use OpenAI tokenizers as a proxy for Claude's, which isn't public.

Accuracy was within noise of JSON and Markdown on single-hop retrieval questions over lists of up to 100 rows, on Claude Haiku, Sonnet and Opus 5.5 and on GPT-6 Sol. It is untested on small or open-weight models, on nested data, on longer lists and on multi-step tasks. Numbers and method: [TOON benchmarks](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi/blob/main/docs/toon-benchmarks.md).

The savings are for flat, uniform lists. On nested data they are roughly neutral: [TOON's own benchmark](https://toonformat.dev/guide/benchmarks) shows about 1.6% more tokens than compact JSON on its mixed-structure datasets. michi's TOON is for models reading tool output, not for models writing it; published evidence shows small models write TOON poorly ([arXiv 2601.12014](https://arxiv.org/abs/2601.12014)).

Output conforms to the [TOON 4.4 specification](https://github.com/toon-format/spec/blob/main/SPEC.md) — every agent-facing block, not just lists: key-value blocks, errors, status, recovery hints and partial-success reports are TOON documents too, so an agent parses one format. Values are quoted only when the spec requires it — a delimiter, colon, bracket, quote, line break, or a value that would otherwise read as a number, boolean or `null` — so the common case carries no quoting overhead.

## Quick start

### Rust

```rust
use michi_core::toon::{render_toon, ToonOptions, Value};

fn main() -> Result<(), Box<dyn std::error::Error>> {
    let opts = ToonOptions::new(
        "issues",
        vec!["number".to_string(), "title".to_string(), "state".to_string()],
        vec![
            vec![Value::Int(51815), Value::from("[Bug]: Telegram plugin"), Value::from("open")],
            vec![Value::Int(51812), Value::from("dark mode request"), Value::from("open")],
        ],
    )
    .total_count(Some(8771))
    .hints(vec!["Run `gh-axi issue view <number>` to view an issue".to_string()]);

    print!("{}", render_toon(&opts)?);
    Ok(())
}
```

### TypeScript / Node.js

```typescript
import { renderToon } from "@orin-dx/michi";

const out = renderToon({
  typeName: "issues",
  fields: ["number", "title", "state"],
  rows: [
    [
      { type: "int", intVal: 51815 },
      { type: "str", strVal: "[Bug]: Telegram plugin" },
      { type: "str", strVal: "open" },
    ],
    [
      { type: "int", intVal: 51812 },
      { type: "str", strVal: "dark mode request" },
      { type: "str", strVal: "open" },
    ],
  ],
  totalCount: 8771,
  hints: ["Run `gh-axi issue view <number>` to view an issue"],
});

process.stdout.write(out);
```

### Output

```text
issues[2]{number,title,state}:
  51815,"[Bug]: Telegram plugin",open
  51812,dark mode request,open
totalCount: 8771
help[1]: Run `gh-axi issue view <number>` to view an issue
```

## Workspace Architecture

`michi` is organized as a Cargo workspace with three published crates. `michi-core` holds every sync primitive and by default depends only on `thiserror` and `compact_str`; `michi-pipeline` adds async execution on `tokio`; `michi-graph` (MIT, no dependencies) validates and orders dependency graphs. Optional features live on `michi-core`:

### Free functions

| Function | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `renderToon` | `(opts: ToonOptions) => string` — TOON list rendering |
| `emptyState` | `(typeName: string) => string` — definitive empty-state block |
| `emptyStateWithHints` | `(typeName: string, hints: string[]) => string` — the empty-state block plus `help[N]: …`; like `emptyState`, throws `toon_validation_failed: …` for a reserved type name (a root key michi writes, such as `help` or `error`) |
| `renderHints` | `(hints: string[]) => string` — the inline array `help[N]: h1,h2` |
| `appendHints` | `(body: string, hints: string[]) => string` — append `help[N]: …` to a document, on its own line |
| `renderRecovery` | `(hints: RecoveryHint[]) => string` — the table `recovery[N]{tool,params,reason}:` (`params` is `"{}"` here; an absent reason is `null`) |
| `renderKv` | `(items: KvItem[], totalCount?: number, hints: string[]) => string` — `key: value` lines; throws `kv_validation_failed: …` for a repeated key or a reserved key (a root key michi writes, such as `help` or `message`) |
| `renderDomainError` | `(code, message, hints, githubAnnotation?, causes?) => string` — `error`, `message`, `causes`, `exit_code`, `help` |
| `renderStatus` | `(toolName, description, items, hints?) => string` — `tool`, `description`, the table `items[N]{key,value,health,reason}:`, `help` |
| `renderAlreadyDone` | `(operation, summary, hints) => string` — `operation`, `status: already_done`, `summary`, `help` |
| `alreadyDone` | `(stored?: string \| null) => { done: boolean, result?: string }` — classify an idempotency lookup: any stored string (even empty) is done |
| `renderPartialSuccess` | `(completed: OpRef[], failed: FailedOp[], skipped: OpRef[]) => string` — the summary, the `completed[N]{index,operation}:`, `failed[N]{index,operation,reason}:` and `skipped[N]{index,operation,reason}:` tables (`index` is the op's position in your batch; a skipped op's `reason` is a machine token, `null` when absent) and the failed ops' `recovery[N]{tool,params,reason}:` table |
| `renderPipeline` | `(steps: PipelineStep[]) => string` — the table `step[N]{id,name,status,reason}:`; `status` is a `StepStatus` label (`completed`, `outcome_unknown`, …) and `reason` is required exactly for `outcome_unknown`, `skipped` and `not_run` |
| `truncate` | `(content: string, maxChars: number) => { content, originalChars, removed, wasTruncated }` — text that fits comes back unchanged; a longer text keeps its first `maxChars - 1` chars and ends in `…`, and the cut is reported in `removed` and `wasTruncated`, never inside `content`. Add your own hint, for example `cut ${removed} of ${originalChars} chars; pass full=true`, to the response's `help[]`. |
| `parseRetryAfter` | `(headerValue: string) => number \| null` — an RFC 9110 `Retry-After` value (delay-seconds or HTTP-date) in seconds; a past date is `0`, a malformed value `null` |
| `nextRetryDelay` | `(maxRetries, baseDelayMs, maxDelayMs, jitterFactor, jitterSeed, attempt, retryAfterMs?) => number \| null` — the next back-off delay in ms, or `null` once retries are used up; pass a random `jitterSeed` in `[0, 1]` per call |
| `isRetryableStatus` | `(status: number) => boolean` — `true` for 429, 502, 503 and 504; retry 502 and 504 only for idempotent requests |

### `AgentResponse` class

The primary integration point — a builder that composes TOON/KV rendering, hints, and recovery into one response.

Setters return `void`, not `this`, so call them as sequential statements rather than a chain. (Chaining isn't supported across the NAPI boundary — see `docs/spec/04-mcp-and-napi.md` in the main repo for why.)

| Method | Signature |
| --- | --- |
| `constructor` | `(typeName: string)` |
| `.items` | `(rows: ToonValue[][], fields: string[], totalCount?: number \| null) => void` — appends a TOON list section named for the response's type; each call adds one, rendered in call order. `totalCount` is how many rows existed before a cut and renders only when it is larger than the rows passed |
| `.kvItems` | `(items: KvItem[], totalCount?: number \| null) => void` — appends a key-value section the same way |
| `.hint` | `(hint: string) => void` |
| `.recoveryHint` | `(tool: string, reason?: string) => void` |
| `.truncationHint` | `(hint: string) => void` — the caller's instruction for getting a cut cell in full (same as `ToonOptions.truncationHint`). Cut cells end in `…` and are listed in a `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block; when a cell was cut, the hint adds one `help[]` line after your own hints. Without it the block still reports each cut |
| `.asError` | `() => void` |
| `.renderText` | `() => string` — the sections in call order, then `help[]` and `recovery[]` |
| `.renderJson` | `() => string` — compact JSON: `{"body":...,"sections":[...],"hints":[...],"recovery":[...],"isError":bool}` |
| `.renderHintsOnly` | `() => string` — just the `help[N]: …` line |
| `.humanContent` | `(text: string) => void` — attach a `user`-audience companion block for `toCallToolResult()` |
| `.hasHumanContent` | `() => boolean` — whether `.humanContent()` was set |
| `.renderFor` | `(audience: "assistant" \| "user") => string` — `"user"` returns the `humanContent` block if set, otherwise the assistant rendering |
| `.toCallToolResult` | `() => CallToolResult` — the MCP `tools/call` response shape: `{content, isError, structuredContent}`, with each content block's `annotations.audience` set correctly |

Full type definitions ship in `index.d.ts`. See the [main repo](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi) for the complete primitive set, the TOON grammar, and the `michi-core` Rust API this wraps (this package always carries the same version as `michi-core`).

## Input and output limits

| `.kvItems` | `(items: KvItem[], totalCount?: number \| null) => void` — appends a key-value section the same way |
| `.hint` | `(hint: string) => void` |
| `.recoveryHint` | `(tool: string, reason?: string) => void` |
| `.truncationHint` | `(hint: string) => void` — the caller's instruction for getting a cut cell in full (same as `ToonOptions.truncationHint`). Cut cells end in `…` and are listed in a `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block; when a cell was cut, the hint adds one `help[]` line after your own hints. Without it the block still reports each cut |
| `.asError` | `() => void` |
| `.renderText` | `() => string` — the sections in call order, then `help[]` and `recovery[]` |
| `.renderJson` | `() => string` — compact JSON: `{"body":...,"sections":[...],"hints":[...],"recovery":[...],"isError":bool}` |
| `.renderHintsOnly` | `() => string` — just the `help[N]: …` line |
| `.humanContent` | `(text: string) => void` — attach a `user`-audience companion block for `toCallToolResult()` |
| `.hasHumanContent` | `() => boolean` — whether `.humanContent()` was set |
| `.renderFor` | `(audience: "assistant" \| "user") => string` — `"user"` returns the `humanContent` block if set, otherwise the assistant rendering |
| `.toCallToolResult` | `() => CallToolResult` — the MCP `tools/call` response shape: `{content, isError, structuredContent}`, with each content block's `annotations.audience` set correctly |

Full type definitions ship in `index.d.ts`. See the [main repo](https://github.com/orin-dx/michi) for the complete primitive set, the TOON grammar, and the `michi-core` Rust API this wraps (this package always carries the same version as `michi-core`).

content.content:
- **Hint wording** is exactly `showing {kept} of {total_before}; {guidance}`, or `showing {kept} of {total_before}` for empty guidance (mirroring `truncate`, which drops its `— use …` clause for an empty hint). `None` when nothing was cut. It reads as a count rather than reusing `truncate`'s `(N more chars — use …)` suffix because it sits next to `totalCount` as its own `help[]` entry, not inside a cell.

michi emits this subset of TOON 4.4. Lines are separated by LF; the document has no trailing newline, no trailing spaces, no blank lines and no byte-order mark (§12).

```
document     ::= list (LF truncated)? (LF totalcount)? (LF help)? (LF recovery)?   (a list document: a root object, §5)
               | entry (LF entry)*                     (any other block: a root object, unique keys, §14.3)
entry        ::= key ": " cell | list | inline | recovery   (primitive field §8, arrays §9)
inline       ::= key "[" count "]: " cell ("," cell)*   (inline primitive array, §9.1)
recovery     ::= "recovery[" count "]{tool,params,reason}:" (LF row)+   (tabular, §9.3)
list         ::= key ": []"                            (no rows, §9.1)
               | key "[" count "]:" (LF "  -")+        (rows with zero fields: empty objects, §9.4/§10)
               | key "[" count "]{" fields "}:" (LF row)+   (tabular, §9.3)
fields       ::= key ("," key)*                        (at least one, all distinct, §6)
row          ::= "  " cell ("," cell)*                 (one cell per field)
cell         ::= string | number | "true" | "false" | "null"
truncated    ::= "truncated[" count "]{row,field,removed}:" (LF "  " digits "," string "," digits)+   (tabular, §9.3)
totalcount   ::= "totalCount: " digits                 (§8)
help         ::= "help[" count "]: " string ("," string)*   (inline primitive array, §9.1)
count        ::= "0" | [1-9][0-9]*                     (equals the number of rows, items or hints)

key          ::= unquoted-key | quoted                 (§7.3)
## Examples

**List response:**

```
issues[3]{number,title,state}:
  42,Fix login redirect,open
  43,Add dark mode,open
  44,"Update deps, bump major",closed
totalCount: 47
help[2]: Call get_issue with number=<number> for full detail,Call list_issues with state=open to filter
```

**Truncated field value** (`.max_cell_len(40).truncation_hint("full=true")`, descriptions of 75 and 73 chars):

```
components[2]{name,description,tokens}:
  Button,Primary action element used to submit f…,12
  Icon,Scalable vector glyphs that inherit col…,8
truncated[2]{row,field,removed}:
  0,description,36
  1,description,34
totalCount: 84
help[2]: Call get_component with name=<name> and full=true for complete description,Cut cells are listed in the truncated block; use full=true for the full value
```

**Empty state:**

```
issues: []
totalCount: 0
help[1]: Try list_issues with a broader filter
```

**Quoted keys, nulls and numbers:**

```
"pull-requests"[2]{id,"head ref",merged_at,score}:
  18446744073709551615,"feature/x:y",null,0.000001
  7,main,"2026-10-21T09:00:00Z",1e+21
```

**Single recovery hint (no list):**

```
recovery[1]{tool,params,reason}:
  create_item,"{\"project\":\"PROJ\",\"type\":\"Task\"}",project is required
```

A dedicated `recovery[N]` table, not folded into `help[]`: hints are strings, recovery hints are records. See [Agent-facing blocks](#agent-facing-blocks) for its columns.

## Agent-facing blocks

Every block michi renders for an agent — not only lists — is a TOON 4.4 root object with the default options, so an agent parses one format. Each renderer returns a finished document with no trailing newline; `append_hints` and `append_recovery` join a block onto a document with exactly one LF (none when the buffer is empty or already ends in one). Composition keeps keys unique: a list's type name and a KV key may not be `totalCount`, `help` or `recovery`, and KV keys may not repeat (`ToonError::InvalidTypeName`, `KvError`). Strings and keys are quoted per [Strings](#strings); numbers follow [Numbers, booleans and null](#numbers-booleans-and-null).

**Key-value (`kv::render_kv`, `AgentResponse` KV sections)** — one `key: value` field per item (§8), exactly one space after the colon (no column alignment), then `totalCount` and `help`:

```
id: abc-123
title: "Fix login: redirect loop"
score: 0.25
wait: 1.5s
assignee: null
totalCount: 1
help[1]: Call update_issue with id=<id>
```

`KvValue::Text` is a string; `Int` and `Bool` are literals; `Float(f, decimals)` is `f` rounded to `decimals` places, written in canonical form (`Float(1.5, 3)` → `1.5`, NaN → `null`); `Duration` is the string `1.5s`; `Missing` is `null`.


## Truncation

A string cell longer than `max_cell_len` chars (default 200) is cut, and the cut is reported out of band, so the cell's own text can never pose as michi's signal:

- The cell keeps its first `max_cell_len - 1` chars and ends with a plain `…`, so a cut cell is exactly `max_cell_len` chars. A cap of 1 gives `…` and a cap of 0 gives the empty string `""`. The cell never carries a message.
- A `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block follows the list and lists every cut cell, in row then field order: `row` is the 0-based row index, `field` the field name, and `removed` the number of chars cut. Kept chars (not counting the `…`) plus `removed` equal the original char count. The block is omitted when nothing was cut. A cell that ends in `…` with no entry in the block is just data.
- When the caller sets `ToonOptions::truncation_hint` (`AgentResponse::truncation_hint`, NAPI `truncationHint`) and a cell was cut, michi adds one line to `help[]`, after the caller's own hints: `Cut cells are listed in the truncated block; use {hint} for the full value`. michi does not know the calling tool's parameters, so it never invents a hint; an empty hint is the same as none. The hint is tool-author text and travels in the trusted `help` channel, not in a cell.
- The cap counts chars **before** escaping and quoting: a cut cell is then quoted and escaped by the rules above, so a cell holding `"`, `\`, a line break or a comma is written longer than `max_cell_len`.
- Numbers, booleans and `null` are never truncated.
- `truncate::truncate()` (and NAPI `truncate`) cuts one free-text string the same way and reports the cut in `Truncated::removed`, not in the text, so the text never carries a message that data could imitate.

## Size limits

`ToonOptions::validate()` rejects a list whose shape would make rendering unreasonably large, before it looks at any row. The limits are public constants in `michi_core::toon`:

| Limit | Constant | Error |
| --- | --- | --- |
| At most 1,000 header fields | `MAX_FIELDS` | `ToonError::TooManyFields { count, max }` |
| At most 1,000,000 cells (`rows × fields`; a list with no fields counts one cell per row) | `MAX_CELLS` | `ToonError::TooManyCells { rows, fields, max }` |
| A `truncation_hint` of at most 256 chars | `MAX_TRUNCATION_HINT_CHARS` | `ToonError::TruncationHintTooLong { len, max }` |

- Checks run in a fixed order and the first failure wins: reserved type name, field count, repeated field, cell count, truncation hint length, row length.
- Every check is linear: repeated field names are found with a set, so the largest accepted header costs 1,000 lookups instead of ~500,000 comparisons.
- serde `list()` checks the field and cell limits against the union of the items' keys before it builds any row, so a sparse item set (each item with a few distinct keys) cannot expand into a huge table of `null` cells.
- `AgentResponse` reports a violation like any other validation failure: an `error: toon_validation_failed` body with `isError` set on the text, JSON and MCP surfaces.

Each renderer returns a finished document with no trailing newline; `append_hints` and `append_recovery` join a block onto a document with exactly one LF (none when the buffer is empty or already ends in one). Composition keeps keys unique: a list's type name and a KV key may not be `totalCount`, `help` or `recovery`, and KV keys may not repeat (`ToonError::InvalidTypeName`, `KvError`). Strings and keys are quoted per [Strings](#strings); numbers follow [Numbers, booleans and null](#numbers-booleans-and-null).

**Key-value (`kv::render_kv`, `AgentResponse` KV sections)** — one `key: value` field per item (§8), exactly one space after the colon (no column alignment), then `totalCount` and `help`:

```
id: abc-123
title: "Fix login: redirect loop"
score: 0.25
wait: 1.5s
assignee: null
totalCount: 1
help[1]: Call update_issue with id=<id>
```

`KvValue::Text` is a string; `Int` and `Bool` are literals; `Float(f, decimals)` is `f` rounded to `decimals` places, written in canonical form (`Float(1.5, 3)` → `1.5`, NaN → `null`); `Duration` is the string `1.5s`; `Missing` is `null`.


## Truncation

A string cell longer than `max_cell_len` chars (default 200) is cut, and the cut is reported out of band, so the cell's own text can never pose as michi's signal:

- The cell keeps its first `max_cell_len - 1` chars and ends with a plain `…`, so a cut cell is exactly `max_cell_len` chars. A cap of 1 gives `…` and a cap of 0 gives the empty string `""`. The cell never carries a message.
- A `truncated[N]{row,field,removed}:` block follows the list and lists every cut cell, in row then field order: `row` is the 0-based row index, `field` the field name, and `removed` the number of chars cut. Kept chars (not counting the `…`) plus `removed` equal the original char count. The block is omitted when nothing was cut. A cell that ends in `…` with no entry in the block is just data.
- When the caller sets `ToonOptions::truncation_hint` (`AgentResponse::truncation_hint`, NAPI `truncationHint`) and a cell was cut, michi adds one line to `help[]`, after the caller's own hints: `Cut cells are listed in the truncated block; use {hint} for the full value`. michi does not know the calling tool's parameters, so it never invents a hint; an empty hint is the same as none. The hint is tool-author text and travels in the trusted `help` channel, not in a cell.
- The cap counts chars **before** escaping and quoting: a cut cell is then quoted and escaped by the rules above, so a cell holding `"`, `\`, a line break or a comma is written longer than `max_cell_len`.
- Numbers, booleans and `null` are never truncated.
- `truncate::truncate()` (and NAPI `truncate`) cuts one free-text string the same way and reports the cut in `Truncated::removed`, not in the text, so the text never carries a message that data could imitate.

## Size limits

`ToonOptions::validate()` rejects a list whose shape would make rendering unreasonably large, before it looks at any row. The limits are public constants in `michi_core::toon`:

| Limit | Constant | Error |
| --- | --- | --- |
| At most 1,000 header fields | `MAX_FIELDS` | `ToonError::TooManyFields { count, max }` |
| At most 1,000,000 cells (`rows × fields`; a list with no fields counts one cell per row) | `MAX_CELLS` | `ToonError::TooManyCells { rows, fields, max }` |
| A `truncation_hint` of at most 256 chars | `MAX_TRUNCATION_HINT_CHARS` | `ToonError::TruncationHintTooLong { len, max }` |

- Checks run in a fixed order and the first failure wins: reserved type name, field count, repeated field, cell count, truncation hint length, row length.
- Every check is linear: repeated field names are found with a set, so the largest accepted header costs 1,000 lookups instead of ~500,000 comparisons.
- serde `list()` checks the field and cell limits against the union of the items' keys before it builds any row, so a sparse item set (each item with a few distinct keys) cannot expand into a huge table of `null` cells.
- `AgentResponse` reports a violation like any other validation failure: an `error: toon_validation_failed` body with `isError` set on the text, JSON and MCP surfaces.

s+='''
### Resolved 2026-11-16 — Legacy removal and render performance

The 0.10.0 audits found one concept written two ways in several places. Pre-1.0, nothing is kept as a shim.

- **`ToonOptions` is the list alone.** `hints`, `total_count` and `truncation_hint` are gone, with their builders, and so are the `render_kv(items, total_count, hints)` and NAPI `renderToon`/`renderKv` parameters that mirrored them. `totalCount`, `help[]` and the truncation hint belong to the composer, which places each once however many sections a response has (a document may hold only one `help` key, which is why the truncation line cannot be added by a standalone renderer). `render_toon` writes the list entry and the `truncated` block for a cut cell; callers who want hints on a standalone list use `append_hints`. `render_kv(items)` writes the `key: value` lines. `AgentResponse::truncation_hint` keeps the 256-char cap (`MAX_TRUNCATION_HINT_CHARS`, `ToonError::TruncationHintTooLong`), now checked by the response. NAPI: `renderToon({typeName, fields, rows})`, `renderKv(items)`; `totalCount` stays on `AgentResponse.items` and `kvItems`, `truncationHint` on `AgentResponse`.
- **One definitive empty state.** `empty_state`, `empty_state_with_hints`, `try_empty_state`, `try_empty_state_with_hints`, the `empty` module and NAPI `emptyState` and `emptyStateWithHints` are deleted. They rendered `name: []` and `totalCount: 0`, while an untouched `AgentResponse` and an empty `Toon` section rendered `name: []` alone, so an agent saw two shapes from one library. The decision is the definitive one: an empty `Toon` section (and so an untouched response) renders `name: []` and `totalCount: 0`, so a reader sees "zero results" and not a list that might have been dropped. A larger `totalCount` the caller set stays as set. An empty `Kv` section still renders nothing: it has no list to be empty. The JSON `sections` entry keeps the caller's facts (`returnedCount: 0`; `totalCount` only when set), so `truncated` stays derived from set total and count. **Output moves (the only ones in this change):** `AgentResponse::new(n)` with nothing added, and a response holding an empty `Toon` section, gain a `totalCount: 0` line; two or more sections that report a total (an empty list now does) merge into the `totalCount[N]{section,total}:` table. A reserved type name still renders the `toon_validation_failed` error block, as `empty_state` did.
- **Render by borrowed view.** `AgentResponse` copied every row into a `ToonOptions` on each validate and each render: 2,015 allocations to render 1,000 rows, 2,011 for `is_error()` and 4,030 for both, against 3 for `render_toon`. `ToonDocument` now validates and renders a borrowed list (`type_name`, `fields`, `rows`, the cell cap and the truncation hint as references), so the response renders what it holds. `tests/alloc_count.rs` counts allocations with a counting allocator (a count is deterministic where time is not) and fails if `render`, `is_error()` or `to_call_tool_result()` costs per row. This closes the "cost accepted" note under "One section model". `toon::list` turns each item into cells as it parses it instead of keeping every parsed object until the rows are built.
- **Module names.** `empty` is gone with its functions. `truncate` (one string) and `truncation` (a list) stay two modules, as "Module:" under the list-truncation decision records; the audit's merge would re-open that decision for no behaviour change. `idempotency` (partial success) keeps its name here: renaming it is part of the API-conventions work.
- **Coverage.** `benches/response_render.rs` times `render`, `render(Json)`, `is_error()` and `to_call_tool_result()`; `tests/scaling.rs` gained `AgentResponse` rows, `to_call_tool_result`/`is_error` and `toon::list` cases.
'''
open(p,'w').write(s)

michi-core: Breaking: `ToonOptions` is the list alone. `hints`, `total_count` and `truncation_hint` (and their builders) are removed; `totalCount`, `help[]` and the truncation hint belong to `AgentResponse`, which places each once for the whole response. `render_toon` writes the list entry and the `truncated` block. `render_kv(items)` lost its `total_count` and `hints` parameters. NAPI: `renderToon` no longer takes `totalCount`, `hints` or `truncationHint`, and `renderKv(items)` no longer takes `totalCount` or `hints`; `AgentResponse.items`, `kvItems` and `truncationHint` keep them.

Migration: `render_toon(&ToonOptions::new(..).total_count(Some(n)).hints(h))` becomes `AgentResponse::new(name).section(Section::toon(name, fields, rows).total_count(Some(n))).hint(..)` rendered with `render(OutputFormat::Text)`. For hints on a standalone list, `append_hints(&mut out, &hints)`.

michi-core: Breaking: one definitive empty state. `empty_state`, `empty_state_with_hints`, `try_empty_state`, `try_empty_state_with_hints`, the `empty` module and NAPI `emptyState` and `emptyStateWithHints` are removed. An empty `Toon` section, and so an untouched `AgentResponse`, now renders `name: []` and `totalCount: 0` (it rendered `name: []` alone). Use `AgentResponse::new(name)` (plus `.hint(..)`) where you called `empty_state`. An empty `Kv` section still renders nothing.

michi-core: `AgentResponse::render`, `is_error()` and `to_call_tool_result()` no longer copy every row on each call. They validate and render a borrowed view of the section's rows: 1,000 rows took 2,015 allocations to render and 2,011 for `is_error()`, and now take about what `render_toon` takes. `toon::list` no longer keeps every parsed item until the rows are built. Output is unchanged.

input.content:
## What

Removes the leftover duplicates the 0.10.0 audits found, and makes `AgentResponse` render without copying its rows. Base is `integration/hardening`.

- **Duplication #4, #11:** `ToonOptions` is the list alone. `hints`, `total_count` and `truncation_hint` are gone, and so are the `render_kv(items, total_count, hints)` and NAPI `renderToon`/`renderKv` parameters that mirrored them. The composer owns `totalCount`, `help[]` and the truncation hint (a document may hold one `help` key). `render_parts(inline)` was already replaced by `render_list`; nothing is left of it.
- **Duplication #6:** one definitive empty state. `empty_state*`, the `empty` module and NAPI `emptyState`/`emptyStateWithHints` are deleted. An empty `Toon` section (and so an untouched `AgentResponse`) renders `name: []` and `totalCount: 0`.
- **Rust-perf #1:** `ToonDocument` validates and renders a borrowed list. `tests/alloc_count.rs` (counting allocator, `stats_alloc` dev-dependency, MIT) failed first at 3,013 allocations to render 1,000 rows against 1,002 for `render_toon`, and passes now.
- **Rust-perf #7:** `toon::list` turns each item into cells as it parses it and no longer keeps every parsed object.
- **Rust-perf #10:** `benches/response_render.rs` (divan) and three scaling cases (response rows, `to_call_tool_result`/`is_error`, `toon::list`).

## Deliberate output change (the only one)

Rendered output is otherwise unchanged; the existing snapshots are the proof. The empty-state decision moves three things:

1. `AgentResponse::new(n)` with nothing added: `n: []` becomes `n: []` + `totalCount: 0`.
2. A response holding an empty `Toon` section gets the same `totalCount: 0` line.
3. Two or more sections reporting a total (an empty list now does) merge into the `totalCount[N]{section,total}:` table.

An empty `Kv` section still renders nothing. The JSON `sections` entry keeps the caller's facts. Spec: `docs/spec/06-decisions.md`, "Resolved 2026-11-16 — Legacy removal and render performance".

## Not done

- Architecture #9: the `truncate`/`truncation` merge would re-open the recorded decision in `06-decisions.md` ("Module: a new `truncation` module beside `truncate`"). `empty` is removed. `idempotency` is in W2-B's files, so I left the rename to them.
- `docs/spec/06-decisions.md-e` is a tracked stray file (a `sed -i` backup); not mine, left alone.

## Call-site fixes outside my files

`crates/michi-core/src/napi.rs` (module table, and the `#[napi]` count floor 30 to 29 because two exports went), `fuzz/fuzz_targets/{toon_render,mcp_wire}.rs`, `scripts/smoke/*`, `AGENTS.md` and `ARCHITECTURE.md` (the `empty` rows), `packages/michi-node` tests and README.

## How checked (exit codes)

`just fmt-check` 0, `just clippy` 0, `just typos` 0, `just test-rust` 0 (874 tests), `just check` 0. In `packages/michi-node`: `pnpm build`, `pnpm test` (177 pass, 0 fail). Mutants, each caught and reverted: cloning rows in `failed_flags` (`alloc_count`), `totalCount` 1 instead of 0 for an empty list (12 tests), a per-row scan in `push_list` (three scaling tests, 92x), writing a cell to column 0 in `toon::list` (6 tests).

Not run: `oxlint --type-aware` exits non-zero on warnings that were there before (template-literal types); the fuzz targets compile (`just fuzz-check`, part of `just check`) but were not run; `just bench` not run.
